# Module 3: Savings

## Introduction

Saving is one of the most important topics in financial literacy. While financial literacy is not limited to encouraging saving, it is impossible to think about financial literacy without discussing the crucial nature of savings. Most women know that saving is essential. But they might now know what savings really mean or how your life can be impacted when you don't have adequate savings. They might be unaware of where they should save and where they should not and why? In this module, we will be studying the answers to all these questions. ## Objectives

- To guide participants to be clear about the crucial nature of savings. - To assist participants to understand that it is more beneficial if they save with a particular goal in mind
- To assist participants to calculate how much one needs to save to achieve a particular goal. **Duration:** 1 hour 45 minutes

## Process

- Exercise 1: Suman's Story: (Part 3)
- Exercise 2: The Meaning of Savings
- Game 1: How do Small Savings Grow? - Exercise 3: Saving Towards Goals
- Exercise 4: Where Should we Save? Where Should we Not Save? - Roleplay 1
- Key Messages
- Closing

# Exercise 1: Suman's Story (Part 3)

**Duration:** 10 minutes

## Process

Suman was very happy the next day. Sunitadidi also was happy to see her. Suman said, "I want to share something with everyone." With Sunitadidi's permission, Suman continued, "I discussed the training with my husband and mother-in-law and talked about the importance of reducing unnecessary expenses. Both of them were willing. We even took a collective decision on which unnecessary expenses we can reduce. As a result, we have been able to save ₹ 500 which I can use to repay the bank installment. We have decided that we will buy milk for the children and vegetables of our family from this month onwards. If our family's health improves, our medical expenses will also reduce automatically. "If I am able to have some money left over, I might be able to even save it. I have a feeling that I will be able to make my dreams a reality. ![img-3.jpeg](img-3.jpeg)

But I do not have any idea about the real meaning of savings and how and where should I save."

Seeing Suman so animated, Sunitadidi was delighted. "Wait...Wait...Let us learn everything one by one," Sunitadidi laughed. 3

## Exercise 2: The Meaning of Saving

### Duration: 10 minutes

- ❖ Ask women to tell you what they think the meaning of saving is along with an example. If their answer is correct, congratulate them. If the answer is not fully correct, tell them the correct answer which is - if expenses are less than income, whatever money remains from the income can be called balance. For example, if your income is ₹ 6,000 and your expenses are ₹ 5,500 then the balance will be ₹ 500. - ❖ If we keep that ₹ 500 aside for our future expenses then it is called savings. - ❖ Our savings are “the money that we keep aside after deducting our expenses from our income to meet our future needs.”
- ❖ Ask the participants, “Which one of you finds it possible to save?” Congratulate them if the answer is correct. If their answer is not completely correct then share the correct answer. - ❖ A person does not have to be wealthy in order to be able to save. Anyone who takes control over their unnecessary expenses and keeps aside at least a small amount for their future needs will be able to save money. Even the

![img-4.jpeg](img-4.jpeg)

poor incur unnecessary expenses such as expenditure on beedis, alcohol, betel leaves, and betel nuts. Some times they feel forced to spend excessively on of cultural and social functions

- ❖ Even a poor person can save a small amount of money. Even small children can save. But they have to reduce or avoid unnecessary expenses. Even a small amount of savings, grows after a certain amount of time. 4

# Game 1: How do Small Savings Grow? **Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** 4 chairs / stools, 60 marbles, 4 small bowls, 15 chocolates, 6 open safety pins, and 10 papers. - ❖ Invite two volunteers to the front of the room. Place 2 chairs / stools on one side and place a bowl with 30 marbles each on each chair. Place two more chairs with one empty bowl on each chair exactly opposite the first pair of chairs at 10' to 12' distance. Ask the volunteers to stand next to one chair each. Now call the first volunteer and tell her that you will count 1, 2 and 3. After you finish counting, she should pick up one marble from the bowl kept on the chair near her, run towards the chair on the opposite side and place the marble in the empty bowl on the chair. She should then return to the first chair, pick up another marble, run towards the opposite chair and place that marble in the empty bowl. She has to continue doing this until you tell her to stop. - ❖ Now ask the second volunteer to do the same thing but only after the first volunteer has placed three marbles in the empty bowl. She should also complete any other tasks which you assign her while doing this exercise – taking a break for the errand before returning to her marbles and bowls. She should also continue until you ask her to stop. ![img-5.jpeg](img-5.jpeg)

- ❖ Start the process by counting 1, 2, and 3. After every 3 marbles are put in the empty bowl put one chocolate in the bowl. - ❖ After the second volunteer places two marbles in her empty bowl, ask her to close the safety pins and after she puts in four marbles, ask her to fold some papers. After she finishes placing six marbles, ask both of them to stop. - ❖ Now calculate the marbles and chocolates in both the bowls. You will find that the first volunteer will have

5

more marbles and chocolates. Ask other participants why this is so. - ❖ The answer will be that the second volunteer started late and kept doing something else in between filling her bowl with marbles. - ❖ Now equate the marbles with savings and the chocolates with interest. - ❖ Ask them what they learned from this game. Make sure you cover the following points:
  - ★ Even if you save a small amount but for a long time, it can grow into a larger pool of money
  - ★ The earlier you start saving, the more you will be able to save and the more interest you will earn
  - ★ If you save consistently, you can save more and earn more interest
  - ★ However, even if you start at a later stage, you can save consistently and grow your savings
- ❖ Now ask them to imagine that each marble is ₹ 5 and one round to one day. If they take seven rounds, it means they have saved ₹ 5 for seven days, and will save ₹ 35 and ₹ 150 in a month, this means they would have saved ₹ 1,875 in a year. The message is clear – even if the amount saved is small, if it is done consistently, it will grow into a significantly larger pool. ![img-6.jpeg](img-6.jpeg)

## Exercise 3: Saving towards Goals

**Duration:** 30 minutes

- ❖ Explain to the women that it is difficult to save when you have no goal in mind, and this can discourage you from continuing to save. However, if you are always aware of your goal, you will be motivated to continue to save money, even if it is difficult. For example, saving for their children's education is an important goal for most women. - ❖ Invite a volunteer to share one of her goals with the group. Ask her to tell the group what she wants to achieve, how much money does she need and how much time she has to achieve her goal. - ❖ For example:
  - ★ Suman's goal: Setting up a small tea shop for her husband to run
  - ★ The amount required: ₹ 15,000. - ★ Time: 3 years
  - ★ If she needs ₹ 15,000 in 3 years, it means she will need ₹ 5,000 in one year and (₹ 15,000 / 3 years = ₹ 5,000) and ₹ 5,000 in 12 months means ₹ 417 in a month (₹ 5000 / 12 months = ₹ 417) and ₹ 13 every day (₹ 417 / 30 days = ₹ 13)

![img-7.jpeg](img-7.jpeg)

- ❖ Similarly, ask a couple of women to calculate how much they need to save in a year/ month/ day. 7

# Exercise 4: Where should we save and where we should not

**Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** Picture cards of bank, post office, self-help group, chit fund, relatives, friends, organization about which we lack information; four card sheets with the following captions:

1. Safe and has scope for growth
2. Safe but has no scope for growth
3. Money may grow but it is not safe
4. Neither safe nor has scope for growth

## Process

- ❖ Explain the meaning of the following two concepts – a) safe and b) scope for growth. - ❖ The places where there is less/ no risk of losing / spending money or getting it stolen can be called safe places. The timely availability of money for meeting the future needs is possible only when money is saved in a safe place. - ❖ The places where interest can be earned on the deposit can be described as places having scope for growth. Due

to inflation, the cost of any product will be much higher after some years than it is today. Hence, if your money does not grow, it will not be sufficient to meet the cost of fulfilling your future needs. It means that it is possible to fight inflation only when the money grows. - ❖ Hence, explain that while saving money one should deposit it only in such places where both these conditions are met. - ❖ Now keep one card sheet each in four corners of the room. Invite seven volunteers and give one picture card each. Tell them that they have to see the card in their hand and decide which of the four adjectives most appropriately describes the picture card. When you say 1, 2, 3 they have to run and stand in the corner where the most appropriate adjective is kept. - ❖ Now call the eighth volunteer and ask her to observe all of them and tell everyone where would she want to deposit her savings and why. - ❖ Now call another volunteer and ask her to observe all of them and tell everyone where would she not want to deposit her savings and why. 8

# Key Messages

## Duration: 10 minutes

- ❖ We are going to revise the key messages of the third module with the help of this flipchart. We have to show each page of the flipchart and try to let the women share the key message / learning based on the pictures in the flipchart. If a participant whom the question is asked is not able to give the correct answer, give a chance to other participants. If none of them is able to answer, ask probing questions, the answers to which can help them provide more information or lead them towards the correct answer. These may include questions starting with words such as who, when, what, why and how etc. - ❖ Despite these efforts if none of the women is able to answer the question, you can provide the answer. However, in that case remember to ensure that all of them have understood the correct answer. - ❖ After opening each page ask women who can read to read out the title. In case if none of them is able to read, you can read it to them and tell that we would be revising the related topic. - ❖ Show the cover page of the flipchart and tell women that we are going to revise what we have learnt in the third module titled Savings. - ❖ Open the second page. Tell women that we are going to revise the meaning of Savings now. - ❖ Now call a woman volunteer and show her the pictures on the page. Ask her to describe each picture and what she understands from it. Ask probing questions if need be. We should get an answer that Balance is what we get when we subtract expenses from the income. If this balance is kept aside in a bank or any other place for a specific purpose of meeting the future needs, it is called savings. - ❖ Now open the third page. Tell women that we are going to revise the benefits received even by saving a small amount of money consistently. - ❖ Now call a woman volunteer and show her the pictures on the page. Ask her to describe each picture and what she understands from it. Ask probing questions if need be. We see in this picture that even if we save ₹ 10 every week at the end of a month i.e. in four weeks, our savings become ₹40. And if we save consistently, in 12 months or in a year it becomes ₹ 480. It shows that even if a small amount is saved regularly it becomes a large sum. - ❖ Now open the fourth page. Tell women that we are going to revise why it is important to save for a goal and how it helps in accruing enough money. Now show the picture to everyone. - ❖ Now call a woman volunteer and show her the pictures on the page. Ask her to describe each picture and what she understands from it. Ask probing questions if need be. 11

## Brief Introduction of the Guide

Mann Deshi is dedicated to the economic empowerment of rural women. It was founded in 1996 in Mhaswad by Chetna Sinha in the drought-prone region of Satara district in Maharashtra. Mann Deshi's vision is to empower women to make their own choices and to be celebrated as equal and valuable members of their families and communities. Our mission is to empower women with the knowledge, skills, courage, access and capital to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. Our model is simple. The Mann Deshi Bank is the country's first cooperative bank set up by and for rural women. Its 8 branches focus on financially excluded and previously unbanked women and provides them with affordable banking services and credit. The Mann Deshi Foundation provides women with the knowledge, skills and support necessary to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. One of the Foundation's flagship programmes is its business schools for rural women and one of its most important courses is financial literacy. We firmly believe that once women are in control of their finances, entire families and communities can and will be transformed. Financial literacy helps women start their financial journeys – building their savings and assets, being able to access affordable credit and fulfilling their goals. Our experience over the last two decades has sharpened our focus and understanding of how to impart effective financial literacy at the grassroots. These are our new, updated and detailed training modules designed especially for field level trainers and include numerous engaging and innovative activities. We are confident that trainers will enjoy using these modules to support women become financially literate and confident. **Your friend and guide**

**Vanita**

**Mann Deshi Foundation**

# Module 4: Bank and Banking Services

## Introduction

India is a country of villages. However, traditionally most of India's poor, and this is especially so of women, have been excluded from formal financial institutions. Indeed, this is why banks like the SEWA Bank of Gujarat and the Mann Deshi Mahila Bank of Maharashtra were set up. Fortunately, things are quite different today. About 80% of India's adults now have access to a bank account. However, access doesn't imply usage or control, and a large number of women in India continue to depend on informal groups and sources for savings and finance. At Mann Deshi we believe that control over financial resources by engaging with the formal financial sector is a key step towards poverty reduction. A Bank is a Government approved and regulated financial institution that provides numerous beneficial affordable services that helps people keep their hard earned money secure, grow their savings, and access affordable loans. This module provides useful information about banks and the services they offer. ## Objectives

- Help women to understand the importance of and provide the information on the necessary documentation required for opening a bank account
- Help women understand the procedure for opening a bank account

- Help women understand the importance of savings accounts and other bank services

**Duration:** 2 hours

## Process

- Exercise 1: Suman's Story (Part 4)
- Exercise 2: What is a Bank? An Overview
- Game 1: Investing Money – Savings Accounts, Recurring Deposits and Fixed Deposits
- Exercise 3: Withdrawing Money from A Bank
- Key Messages
- Closing

# Exercise 1: Suman's Story (Part 4)

**Duration:** 25 minutes

## Process

Suman reached the training very early and waited for Sunitadidi to arrive. When Sunitadidi arrived, she asked Suman, "How come you have come so early today?" Suman replied, "I was excited to learn something new today. Since you told us yesterday about the benefits of keeping our money in the bank, I have been very curious to know more about the bank. Till now, I've only had a bank loan and suffered because of the problem of not being able to make my repayments in time."

Suman continued, "I've always been afraid of my bank and the officers working there. But yesterday my husband told me that he also has a savings account in the bank and he had deposited some money in it. That is how he was able to get a loan from the bank. Now I want to understand the bank with new eyes."

- ❖ Now ask whether anyone has been to a bank and congratulate those who have. Tell those who haven't that one they complete this module, they will also have the confidence to go to a bank. - ❖ Explain that a bank is an organization that is regulated by the Government of India. At a Bank, anyone can open an

![img-4.jpeg](img-4.jpeg)

![img-5.jpeg](img-5.jpeg)

account. Depositing money in a bank account ensures its safety and also earns an interest. Moreover, banks offer many other services. - ❖ Tell the group that you will give them information on all these services in this module. 3

## Exercise 2: What is a Bank? An Overview

**Duration:** 30 minutes

**Training material:** Chits, Samples of K.Y.C.$^{1}$ documents, Passbook, Cheque book, Pay-in slip, Withdrawal slip, A.T.M. card etc. - ❖ You have to play the role of a bank officer. Alternatively, you can invite a Mann Deshi Bank representative from your area to provide information about a bank to the participants. - ❖ Invite seven women to be volunteers. Give them the chits and ask them that to ask questions based on the topic written on the chit to the bank officer. (If you are playing the role of the bank officer, you will have to answer all the questions. For your convenience, the answers of all the questions are provided at the end of this module). - ★ What is a bank account? What are different types of accounts and which one is suitable for participants? (Savings or current)
  - ★ Can anyone open a bank account? How is an account opened? What documents need to be submitted to open an account? (Show the samples of KYC documents)
  - ★ Is it necessary to deposit money while opening an account? - ★ After opening an account what does the bank give

you? (Passbook, cheque book, pay-in slip, withdrawal slip, A.T.M. card etc.)

- ★ What are the benefits of keeping money in a bank account? - ★ What is the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojna? What are the different benefits of this scheme? What is the meaning of B.S.B.D.A. account? - ★ What is the meaning of a B.C.? What is the function of a B.C.? What is the benefit of a B.C. for the account holder? Tell the participants that simply opening an account in a bank is not particularly useful unless it is used. We should use our bank account for the following functions

- ❖ Keeping our money safely
- ❖ Investing and growing our money
- ❖ Withdrawing our money whenever required
- ❖ Transferring money to another party
- ❖ Taking affordable debt
- ❖ Using the overdraft facility
- ❖ Using an A.T.M. card as well as mobile banking

![img-6.jpeg](img-6.jpeg)

$^{1}$ Know Your Customer (K.Y.C.)

# Game 1: Investing Money – Savings Accounts, Recurring Deposits and Fixed Deposit Accounts

**Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** Three cardboard boxes, Play money, ₹ 100: 40 notes, ₹ 10: 35 notes, ₹ 1: 20 notes. - ❖ Invite a volunteer. Place a box in front of her and ask her to pretend the box is her savings account. Tell her that whenever she wants, she can deposit and withdraw money. Ask her to deposit some play money and withdraw it when she requires. Now ask her to count the money that remains in her account after 12 months,
- ❖ Now place the second box in front of her and ask her that to pretend this box is her Recurring Deposit account. Now tell her that, as a depositor, she can deposit a fixed amount every month for a defined period of time, such as one year or two years. For example, ask her to deposit ₹ 100 of play money for every month. Remind her (and the group) that is essential to deposit the amount on a regular basis. Once deposited, this money cannot be until the agreed upon term is over. Also, one needs to deposit money at least for 12 months. After 12 months, your deposit would be ₹ 1200 and at the end of the 12 months' term, you will this ₹ 1200 plus an interest (approximately ₹ 46). The interest is is compound interest calculated on a

![img-7.jpeg](img-7.jpeg)

quarterly basis. This type of account is better for individuals who get a fixed or regular income every month. - ❖ Now place a third box in front of the group and tell them to pretend that this is their fixed deposit account. In this type of an account, you have to invest a fixed lump sum amount for a predefined period. This amount cannot be withdrawn before this period is over. You have to invest the amount only once and this type of investment is a good option for those who get income only once in a year. If you don't withdraw the money from the fixed deposit amount, you can also get a fixed monthly income. If you deposit ₹ 1200 in a fixed deposit, it will grow to ₹ 1200 + interest (approximately ₹ 84) by the end of the year. - ❖ If you wish, you can withdraw your interest every month, or once in three months, in a fixed deposit account. You can also add it to your investment. Compare these three accounts and discuss which account is suitable for different types of individuals. 5

text:
## Question and Answers

1. What is a bank account? What are the different types of accounts? Which is the most suitable account for us? (Savings or current)

- ★ A Bank Account is where we can deposit and withdraw money in a bank. There are different types of accounts and the most suitable account is a Savings Bank Account because it gives us the best interest for our savings while allowing us to withdraw money – up to a limit – as well. - ★ A Current Account is more suitable for entrepreneurs because there is no limit on the number of times one can transact through this account. However, it does not earn any interest. 2. Can anyone open a bank account? How is an account opened? Which documents need to be submitted to open a bank account? (Show the samples of KYC documents)
- ★ Any Indian citizen above 10 years of age can open a bank account. - ★ In the case of those who are less than 10 years old, a joint account can be opened along with that person's parents. - ★ It is important to submit age and address proof which includes documents such as a passport, voters' ID card, Driving license, Aadhaar Card, Pan Card, MGNREGA card etc. In addition we have to submit two copies of recent photograph. 3. Is it necessary to deposit money while opening an account? - ★ You have to deposit an initial amount in all accounts except those accounts opened under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana. ![img-11.jpeg](img-11.jpeg)

7

text:
4. After opening an account what does the bank give you? (Passbook, cheque book, pay-in slip, withdrawal slip, A.T.M. card etc.)

★ Once we open an account, a bank gives us a passbook and A.T.M. card. If we keep the minimum essential balance in our account, we can also get a cheque book. 5. What are the benefits of keeping money in an account? ★ The money you deposit is safe and also attracts interest. In addition, it allows you to benefit from the many other services a bank offers. 6. What is the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojna? What are the different benefits of this scheme? What is the meaning of a B.S.B.D.A. account? ★ The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojna is a scheme started by the Government of India as a part of its efforts towards Financial Inclusion. Under this scheme, it is possible to open a zero balance account. Indian citizens who do not have the documents required under K.Y.C. (Know Your Customer) also can open their bank account by providing 2 copies of photographs. This account is known as B.S.B.D.A. account. The account holder has to submit all the necessary documents within one year. ![img-12.jpeg](img-12.jpeg)

7. What is the meaning of a B.C.? What is the function of a B.C.? What is the benefit of a B.C. for the account holder? ★ B.C. stands for Business Correspondent. This is a service for those account holders, especially those who live in remote villages, to be able to receive certain banking services right at their doorsteps. This is usually made available in those villages which don't have a bank branch and as a result, the B.C. provides all these bank services such as opening an account, depositing and withdrawing money, taking a loan etc. 8

Duration: 20 minutes

- We are going to revise the key messages of the **fourth** module with the help of this flipchart. We have to show each page of the flipchart and try to let the women share the key message / learning based on the pictures in the flipchart. If a participant whom the question is asked is not able to give the correct answer, give a chance to other participants. If none of them is able to answer, ask probing questions, the answers to which can help them provide more information or lead them towards the correct answer. These may include questions starting with words such as who, when, what, why and how etc. - Despite these efforts if none of the women is able to answer the question, you can provide the answer. However, in that case remember to ensure that all of them have understood the correct answer. - After opening each page ask women who can read to read out the title. In case if none of them is able to read, you can read it to them and tell that we would be revising the related topic. - Show the **cover page** of the flipchart and tell women that we are going to revise what we have learnt in the **fourth** module titled **'Bank and Banking Services'**. - Open the **second** page. Tell women that as we can see a bank office where bank officials are giving services to the account holders. - Open the third page. Tell women that here we will revise what we have learnt about opening a bank account. Now we will see the three steps on opening an account. - Now show the picture in the first row to everyone. - Invite a woman volunteer and show her the pictures from the first row. Ask her to describe each picture and what she understands from it. Ask probing questions if need be. The pictures provide information about the first step in opening a bank account which is 'collecting the required documents'. These documents include the age and address proof of the account holder. These could be voters' ID card, Aadhaar Card, Pan Card, MGNREGA job card, passport or driving license. Along with the documents the account holder needs to submit two copies of his/her recent photographs. 10

## Brief Introduction of the Guide

Mann Deshi is dedicated to the economic empowerment of rural women. It was founded in 1996 in Mhaswad by Chetna Sinha in the drought-prone region of Satara district in Maharashtra. Mann Deshi's vision is to empower women to make their own choices and to be celebrated as equal and valuable members of their families and communities. Our mission is to empower women with the knowledge, skills, courage, access and capital to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. Our model is simple. The Mann Deshi Bank is the country's first cooperative bank set up by and for rural women. Its 8 branches focus on financially excluded and previously

unbanked women and provides them with affordable banking services and credit. The Mann Deshi Foundation provides women with the knowledge, skills and support necessary to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. One of the Foundation's flagship programmes is its business schools for rural women and one of its most important courses is financial literacy. We firmly believe that once women are in control of their finances, entire families and communities can and will be transformed. Financial literacy helps women start their financial journeys – building their savings and assets, being able to access affordable credit and fulfilling their goals. Our experience over the last two decades has sharpened our focus and understanding of how to impart effective financial literacy at the grassroots. These are our new, updated and detailed training modules designed especially for field level trainers and include numerous engaging and innovative activities. We are confident that trainers will enjoy using these modules to support women become financially literate and confident. **Your friend and guide**

**Vanita**

**Mann Deshi Foundation**

# Module 5: Debt

## Introduction

Some people's hearts race just on hearing the word 'debt'. They assume debt means a family's financial ruin. But it is important to know when and how loans are necessary and beneficial. It is equally important to be aware of how to make sure that debt is managed responsibly. ![img-3.jpeg](img-3.jpeg)

## Objectives

This module discusses many of these issues

- To clearly understand what debt means and the right reasons to borrow money
- To clearly differentiate between good and bad debt
- To clearly understand the necessary precautions that need to be put in place before taking on debt
- To clearly understand how to responsibly manage debt

**Duration:** 2 hours 25 minutes

## Process

- Exercise 1: Suman's story (Part 5)
- Game 1: Why do we need to take debt? - Exercise 2: Suman's story (Next part)
- Game 2: Good debt and bad debt
- Exercise 3: Important precautions before taking loan
- Game 3: Is it possible to repay the following debt? - Role play: Proper use of Debt
- Key messages
- Closing

text:
# Exercise 1: Suman's Story (Part 5)

**Duration:** 10 minutes

## Process

"Sunitadidi, until today you have been educating us so well. So why suddenly are you talking about debt? Please tell us about something positive," requested Suman, her eyes full of tears. "Suman," Sunitadidi responded gently, "I know that your family loans have caused you a great deal of pain. But it is incorrect to assume that tall debt is bad. Today I will talk to you about responsible debt."

## Let us first understand what debt means. - ❖ Ask the women to explain what debt means to them. Try to understand their answers and write all their important points on the board. After everyone has answered, give them the following definition of debt. - ❖ When we are unable to meet our individual, family or business needs from our income or savings, we are often forced to borrow money for a certain time period. This is debt. It can be with or without interest. ![img-4.jpeg](img-4.jpeg)

- ❖ Explain to the women that this clearly states that the concept of debt comprises the following points
  - ★ We have taken debt in a time of need
  - ★ The money we received in the form of debt does not belong to us
  - ★ We are responsible to repay this loan

3

text:
# Game 1: Why do we Need to Take Debt? **Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** Picture cards having pictures of the various purposes of debt

- Tell the women that they should think about why people need loans. - Ask each of them to talk about why people take on debt - based on their own experiences. Give them a corresponding picture card which represents the reason they raise. If the corresponding card is not available, write the reason on a blank card and give it to woman who raised that issue. Now ask everyone to stand displaying their respective cards. Refer to these cards and reiterate that there are many reasons why people need loans. - Now tell the women who are standing to take a step forward if they feel that any of the reasons displayed on the cards might apply to them one day. - Now ask women to answer the following questions:
- If we are aware that these incidents might happen to us, what should we be doing? Shouldn't we be saving enough money to make sure that we don't need such a loan? Or at least need a smaller loan? ![img-5.jpeg](img-5.jpeg)

- Tell the women to form two groups – the first group will consist of women who feel that they can easily repay a loan and the other will consist of women who are unsure of how to repay a loan. - Now ask the first group to share why they feel so confident. And ask the second group why they are unsure. Thank both the groups and ask them to take their respective seats. 4

path: Financial Literacy/English Financial Literacy/English - Financial Literacy Module/5. V2_English FLT Sub Module 5_DEBT Web File_SJ20200916.pdf
filename: 5. V2_English FLT Sub Module 5_DEBT Web File_SJ20200916.pdf
text:
## Brief discussion

Now discuss the points that have emerged from the game. Ask the group which loans are easier to repay and in which loans are more challenging. Check their answers. If their answers are correct, congratulate them. If the answer is not correct, give them the correct answer. Describe the following difference. ![img-6.jpeg](img-6.jpeg)

- ❖ If we borrow money to start a business or enhance our income then it is easier to repay a loan from the income generated by the business. Examples include loans for starting a vegetable vending business, buying a cow to sell milk, purchasing a vehicle for transporting material etc. - ❖ Now ask the group whether a family suffers when a borrower is able to easily repay their loan,
  - ★ Now explain that if someone borrows money for their household expenses or for some personal reasons, it is more difficult to repay that loan since it does not generate any income. Examples include loans to cover wedding expenses, festival expenses, purchasing luxury items or items for the household use etc. In this case, the borrower is more likely to default because of her inability to pay off regular installments. This will increase the loan burden and it's possible that this can plunge the family into crisis, such as the loss of property, damage of reputation and depression. Therefore, it is important to remember that one should only take a non productive (non income earning) loan only when its absolutely essential. These include illness or essential house repairs. In these cases, regular savings eases the pressure of taking these loans and also the amount one needs to take. 5

★ Now ask the women which loan is good and which is bad and why? ★ Debt for generating / increasing income is good debt because it is easy to repay and does not negatively affect a family. ★ Debt to meet household expenses or fulfill personal wants is bad debt because it does not generate any income and is more difficult to repay. Families often face a number of problems when they are unable to make or delay payments. ![img-7.jpeg](img-7.jpeg)

# Game2: Good and Bad Debt

**Duration:** 15 minutes

**Training material:** A board on which 'Good' is written and another board on which 'Bad' is written. ## Process

- ❖ Divide women into two groups. Give two boards to each group. One of them would have 'Good' written on it and the other will have 'Bad' written on it. Tell them that you will read different examples where different individuals have taken loans for different purposes. After you read each example, the participants have to think whether the particular loan is good or bad and show the board that has their answer. Explain that for every example, different women from each group have to answer. Hence, once the answer is shared the woman has to pass on the board to the next woman in the group. - ❖ Now read the examples one after the other. The respective women have to show the appropriate

![img-8.jpeg](img-8.jpeg)

board after giving a thought to it. The group will get 1 mark if its member shows the board which has the correct answer before the other and is able to justify her answer. - ❖ The game will continue till all examples are over. At the end, sum up all marks of both the groups and announce the winner. 7

## Exercise 2: Suman's Story (Next part)

### Duration: 5 minutes

Suman asked, "Didi, my husband had taken a loan to dig a bore well. It was meant to enhance our income. Then why did we face problems?" Sunitadid replied, "Suman the purpose for which you took on debt was certainly important. At the same time, it is equally important how we utilize this debt. You did use it for a productive purpose but you had not checked out the spot first to ascertain how far down the water table was,"

"Yes...we have decided the spot with the help of a coconut," Suman answered. Sunitadidi continued, "A number of affordable scientific methods are available today that give us pretty accurate information. Moreover, you ended up taking a second loan to continue digging from a money lender. Did you ask him about what his interest rate was or whether it would be charged monthly or annually?"

![img-9.jpeg](img-9.jpeg)

"No we didn't. We should have. We were so grateful that he was ready to give us loan when we needed it," Suman replied, lost in her thoughts. "Don't worry. We will understand all these things today," Sunitadidi said comforting Suman. 8

## Exercise 3: Important Precautions before Taking Loan

**Duration:** 20 minutes

- ❖ Tell the women that they will now need to understand what precautions they should follow and what information they need to make sure they are clear about before taking any debt. - ❖ Invite a volunteer to come to the front of the room. Ask her to play the role of a woman who needs a loan. - ❖ Tell her that you will ask her some questions. She should know the answers to all these questions before she can take the loan. If she knows the answer, she should tell the group. If she does not know the answer, she should tell the group that she doesn't know the answer. - ❖ Ask her the following questions. In case she does not know the answer to a particular question, discuss the consequence of the lack of this information. If she knows the answer, discuss why this information is required. - ★ Why are you taking this loan? (To generate income/ to increase income/ to fulfill your personal needs.)
  - ★ Are you aware that if you take this loan then you have to repay it? - ★ Will you be able to pay the loan installments from the amount which remains after subtracting your expenses from your income? Are you going to get any income from this loan? If yes... will it be enough to pay the installment? From whom will you be taking this loan? (Moneylender/ Bank/ MFI)
- ★ Will you have to provide any collateral for this loan? If yes...are you aware that it might be confiscated if you are unable to repay your loan? Also, if you have to provide collateral, are you aware that the interest rate should be low? - ★ What is the rate of interest for your loan? Is it charged on an annual or monthly basis? (Many moneylenders charge monthly interest, and while the monthly rate might seem low, in fact, it is very high. When a moneylender charges 5% interest rate, it sounds lower than a 10% or 12% annual rate but in fact, it is a 60% annual interest rate. 9

## Game 3: Is it Possible to Repay the following Debt? **Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** Laminated cards of the examples of Debt

### Process

- ❖ Divide women into 8 groups. Give one laminated card to each group and ask them to think whether it is possible for the person depicted in their respective cards to repay his/her debt. They also have to justify their answers. Explain that for answering this question, they need to consider the following points:

- ★ Will the balance i.e. money that remains after covering all the expenses from the income, be sufficient for repaying the loan installment? If the installment is less than the balance, repayment is possible. But if it is more than the balance, the person who has taken the loan would not be able to pay the installment and would be in trouble. ![img-11.jpeg](img-11.jpeg)

- ★ Is he/ she borrowing money for generating income? If yes... it will be easy to pay the loan installment from the additional income generated by the business. - ★ Will the sum of the additional income and balance remaining from income be sufficient to repay the loan installment? If the answer is yes then repayment is possible, otherwise it is difficult. 11

## Brief Introduction of the Guide

Mann Deshi is dedicated to the economic empowerment of rural women. It was founded in 1996 in Mhaswad by Chetna Sinha in the drought-prone region of Satara district in Maharashtra. Mann Deshi's vision is to empower women to make their own choices and to be celebrated as equal and valuable members of their families and communities. Our mission is to empower women with the knowledge, skills, courage, access and capital to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. Our model is simple. The Mann Deshi Bank is the country's first cooperative bank set up by and for rural women. Its 8 branches focus on financially excluded and previously unbanked women and provides them with affordable banking services and credit. The Mann Deshi Foundation provides women with the knowledge, skills and support necessary to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. One of the Foundation's flagship programmes is its business schools for rural women and one of its most important courses is financial literacy. We firmly believe that once women are in control of their finances, entire families and communities can and will be transformed. Financial literacy helps women start their financial journeys – building their savings and assets, being able to access affordable credit and fulfilling their goals. Our experience over the last two decades has sharpened our focus and understanding of how to impart effective financial literacy at the grassroots. These are our new, updated and detailed training modules designed especially for field level trainers and include numerous engaging and innovative activities. We are confident that trainers will enjoy using these modules to support women become financially literate and confident. **Your friend and guide**

**Vanita**

**Mann Deshi Foundation**

# Module 6: Insurance

## Introduction

Our lives are often beset by sudden and unexpected crises such as death, disability or accident of a family member, house damage, crop failure, theft, fire or business collapse. These events not only have severe psychological implications, but serious financial ones that impact everyone in our family. They can drain our hard earned savings. These financial losses can be devastating, wiping out our dreams and money. If we do not have adequate money in savings to meet these emergencies, it is quite possible that we are forced to take high interest loans which are difficult to pay back and increase our vulnerability. There is a way to protect yourself from this – buying insurance. If you have bought insurance, then, if any of the events that you have ensured against occur, the Insurance Company protects you against being financially ruined by the related expenses. No doubt, insurance is essential to help you on your path towards financial security, control and well-being. In this module, we will learn about insurance. ## Objectives

Help participants in understanding the following. - ❖ What is insurance? Why do we need it? - ❖ What are the different types of insurance? Which types of insurance protect against different risks? **Duration:** 2 hours 20 minutes

## Process

- ❖ Exercise 1: Suman's story (Part 6)
- ❖ Exercise 2: Kisan Credit Card
- ❖ Game 1: What is insurance? - ❖ Exercise 3: Introduction to insurance
- ❖ Game 2: Types of Insurance
- ❖ Game 3: True or False
- ❖ Exercise 4: Precautions that should be taken while buying insurance
- ❖ Exercise 5: Important Government insurance schemes
- ❖ Key messages
- ❖ Closing

# Exercise 1: Suman’s Story (Part 6)

**Duration:** 10 minutes

## Process

A storm of thoughts swirled around in Suman’s mind as she walked home after the training session. Until today she had blamed her poor fate for the debt and the financial situation of her family was facing. Now for the very first time, she started wondering that perhaps somewhere along the way, her husband and she had made some unfortunate mistakes, because of their ignorance, which had made things worse. She decided that from that day forward, she would not blame her fate or luck but analyse her situation better and make informed decisions. As she sat down to eat dinner with her husband, she saw that he was lost in thought. “What are you thinking about?” she asked. “Every day, after your training, you come home with so many new ideas. I realize now that we haven’t spent enough time thinking through anything before deciding on a course of action,” replied Ganesh. “I haven’t told you this but last year, Sriram had approached the Gram Panchayat office to tell everyone to survey their lands before deciding where to dig a bore well but I did not follow this advice because

I thought it was an unnecessary expense. Now I feel so guilty,” continued Ganesh with tears in his eyes as Suman tried to reassure him. The next day, on her way to the training, Suman bumped into her neighbour, also a farmer. While things were not as bad as they were for Suman’s family, he had certainly suffered, but things appeared more positive. He told Suman he was on his way to Satara to buy seeds. Suman enquired, “Brother, you need money for seeds. How have you arranged for it?”

“I have a Kisan Credit card now, so I don’t need to worry about that,” he replied. “Which card? What is it?,” Suman asked. Unfortunately, before he could answer, his bus arrived. “I will tell you in the evening,” he said as he hurried away. Suman was still wondering about the credit card when she reached the training. “What is a Kisan Credit Card? How does it solve money problems?” When she saw Sunitadidi, she asked, “Didi, What is this Kisan Credit Card and why didn’t you tell us about this magic wand that solves money problems?”

“That’s exactly what we are going to learn about today, Sunitadidi smiled. 3

## Exercise 2: Kisan Credit Card

**Duration:** 15 minutes

**Training material:** Sample of Kisan Credit Card, Flex of Kisan Credit Card. - Show the sample of Kisan credit card to women. Inform them that since 1998, similar credit cards are issued to farmers in India. The card is issued to both types of farmers, those who have lands in their name and even those who have taken lands on rent. - Now ask women to list out different reasons for which the farmers might need loan. Ensure that the following are included in the list. If some of the reasons from the list are not shared by the women, try to ask probing questions to get the desired answers. The purposes should include the following:
  - Purchasing seeds during the sowing season
  - Purchasing fertilizers and pesticides
  - Purchasing / repairing agricultural tools and equipment
  - Payment of labour charges during harvesting
  - Marketing expense
  - Working capital
  - Capital for starting side / allied businesses
  - Household expenses

![img-3.jpeg](img-3.jpeg)

- Now ask if the same farmer has all these needs in the same year or different farmers have different needs. The answer would be that there is a possibility that the same farmer might experience all these needs for the same crop in the same year. Hence the card holder can use the same card for all these needs. He/she can borrow up to Rs.3, 00,000 in the same year as per his/her requirement. He / she does not need to apply for borrowing money every time he / she needs money. He / she can return the borrowed amount whenever possible to him/her (for example, after selling the crop) but within three years. - Now put up the Kisan Card Flex on the board. Ask women to read the elements one after the other. Ensure that everyone understands them. 4

## Suman’s Story (Next part)

Hearing about the Kisan Credit Card, tears started to roll down Suman’s cheeks. Nirmala, who was sitting beside her said, “Sunitadidid, Suman is crying. She asked you to tell about the Kisan Credit Card and now she is crying.”

Sunitadidi said, “I can understand Suman’s situation. She probably feels that she might not have faced so many of her financial problems if she had known about the card earlier. Suman, you said that you will change things going forward. Better late than never.”

Sunitadidi continued, “I want to add one more thing. Anyone who has this card also gets individual accident insurance which covers them for death or disability due to an accident. Any farmer, whose is less than 70 years old, gets this insurance. The insurance is for three years and the holder has to pay an annual installment of ₹ 5 while the bank adds an additional ₹ 10 every year. The farmer can also get crop insurance in addition to this accident insurance.”

Suman wiped off her tears and asked, “Didi, what is the meaning of insurance? Where can we get it? What are its benefits?”

Suman’s excited flood of questions made Sunitadidi laugh, “This is our usual Suman. She wants to learn everything Okay... let us discuss what exactly insurance is.”

# Game 1: What is Insurance? **Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** Folded chits – Some of them will have the symbol ✓ while the others will not have any sign, picture cards of events which cause financial loss. ## Process

- ❖ Ask everyone to pick up a chit. They should keep the chit with them and not open it. - ❖ Now tell one by one of them to pick up one picture card and see the picture. If the picture refers to a picture that causes financial loss they have to come and stand on the left side. Ask them to come back and take their seat if there is no financial loss. - ❖ After all of them have seen the pictures; ask the women standing on the left side to show their respective pictures and describe the event in the picture. Ask them to describe the kind of financial loss they may suffer if a similar event takes place in their real life. - ❖ Now tell everyone to open and see their chits. Explain that all the women who have chits having '✓' symbol are safe. They have bought insurance that covers the financial loss that takes place if the respective event takes place. It means that the insurance company will make up for their financial loss. - ❖ Explain that those women whose chit does not have the '✓' symbol, are not safe. It means that as they have no insurance, they have to bear their own financial loss. Continue the game till the picture cards are over. - ❖ After the game is over, ask women to share their learning from the game. In case required, you can give them a hint. Certain unexpected events take place in our life. If we are not prepared, the result may be financial loss. Clarify that as insurance covers this financial loss, there is no need to avail loan and hence avoid devastation. - ❖ Tell them that we will try to understand insurance now. 6

## Exercise 3: Introduction to Insurance

**Duration:** 10 minutes

- ❖ Ask the women if any one of them has or had insurance. If any of them have or had taken insurance, ask them to share what insurance means. - ❖ If you are satisfied with their answer, congratulate them and reiterate the meaning. If not, give them the following explanation. - ❖ The agreement between an insurance company and a policy holder is called an insurance policy. According to this agreement, the person who takes insurance pays a small amount of money (an installment or premium) periodically to protect them against a particular event (fire, accident, disability, hospitalization, death). If the event occurs, either the entire or a significant part of the costs associated with that event are paid by the insurance company. - ❖ If you have taken insurance, you can get a tax exemption on the income equivalent to your installment. ![img-5.jpeg](img-5.jpeg)

- ❖ The insurance policy can also be used as collateral against a loan. In such a case you need to enter into an agreement with the insurance company to pay a certain lump sum. In case you default on your loan, the insurance company will pay the bank. - ❖ We can buy insurance from an insurance company, a bank or another financial institution. 7

## Game 2: Types of Insurance

**Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** 3 sets of picture cards of events which cause financial loss (from previous game), 3 sets of picture cards of types of insurance, flex with types of insurance. - ❖ Divide women into three groups. Give each group a set of picture cards of both types. Tell them that if we want to avoid the financial loss from the events seen in the earlier game, we have to buy insurance. Tell them to match the picture cards of events with appropriate type of insurance. - ❖ Ask each group to explain two events and suitable insurance cards. We should get answer that the following types of insurances must be bought to make up for the financial loss due to the respective causes such as
  - ★ Cattle insurance is for covering the financial loss of death of cattle
  - ★ Health insurance is for covering the medical expenses incurred due to illness
  - ★ Accident insurance is to cover the financial loss due to physical injury, death or disability as a result of accident
  - ★ Wealth insurance is to cover the financial loss due to theft, fire and flood etc

- ★ Crop insurance is to cover financial loss due to famine, surplus rainfall, pest and insect attack etc. to the crop
- ★ Vehicle insurance is for covering the financial loss due to damage to the vehicle. - ❖ Now put the flex on the board and ask participants to name the main categories of Insurance they can see. We should get the answer that there are two major types – Life Insurance and General Insurance. Now ask them to look at the flex and tell them different types of insurances that come under the general insurance which we have learnt. Moreover, they should also share the necessity of buying the particular insurance. It should include cattle insurance, wealth insurance, health insurance, vehicle insurance, accident insurance and crop insurance etc. - ❖ Apart from these there is another insurance which covers the financial loss due to the death of an earning member of the family. Explain that the insurance company covers the financial loss if the policy holder dies between the period from buying the insurance to its maturity and hands over the sum assured to the heir (nominee) of the policy holder. 8

## Game 3: True or False

**Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** Laminated card having different statements

### Process

- Tell women that you will read some statements one after the other. They have to understand the meaning properly and tell if the statement is true or false. They also need to justify their answer. - Read the statement and ask one of the women to share her thought. If that particular woman is not able to answer correctly, you can ask other women or provide a hint. If none of them is able to answer despite efforts, share the answer yourself. However, in that case, ensure that everybody understands it. 9

# Exercise 4: Precautions that should be taken while buying insurance

**Duration:** 10 minutes

**Training material:** Samples of documents

- ❖ Explain that one must consider several issues before buying insurance such as
  - ★ Is the insurance company approved by IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)? - ★ Which documents are necessary? For example, Aadhaar Card or proof of age and address, details of income, photograph and salary slip. - ★ What is covered by insurance and what is not? For example, in the case of health insurance, are pregnancy and related conditions included in the cover or not? - ★ Usually, general insurance is only for a period of one year. Hence it is important to know when the insurance will begin and end. You need to remember that there can be no cover if the incident occurs even one day after the expiry date. Hence it is important to renew your policy before it expires. - ★ What is the value of the cover or how much money will you get if the incident takes place? How much money do we have to pay as an installment (premium) to get this amount of cover? - ★ It is important to think about whom you are going to nominate in the case of an incident occurring because they will receive a large amount if the incident occurs. - ★ It is important to realise that the insurance amount will not be automatically transferred to your account. Instead, you will need to submit a claim. Until you do not submit the necessary documents and claim, you will not receive the insurance amount, despite paying all your installments for the insurance. - ★ You know where you should submit your claim, the number of days after the incident within which you need to submit your claim, and which documents do you need to submit to make the claim. ![img-6.jpeg](img-6.jpeg)

## Brief Introduction of the Guide

Mann Deshi is dedicated to the economic empowerment of rural women. It was founded in 1996 in Mhaswad by Chetna Sinha in the drought-prone region of Satara district in Maharashtra. Mann Deshi's vision is to empower women to make their own choices and to be celebrated as equal and valuable members of their families and communities. Our mission is to empower women with the knowledge, skills, courage, access and capital to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. Our model is simple. The Mann Deshi Bank is the country's first cooperative bank set up by and for rural women. Its 8 branches focus on financially excluded and previously unbanked women and provides them with affordable banking services and credit. The Mann Deshi Foundation provides women with the knowledge, skills and support necessary to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. One of the Foundation's flagship programmes is its business schools for rural women and one of its most important courses is financial literacy. We firmly believe that once women are in control of their finances, entire families and communities can and will be transformed. Financial literacy helps women start their financial journeys – building their savings and assets, being able to access affordable credit and fulfilling their goals. Our experience over the last two decades has sharpened our focus and understanding of how to impart effective financial literacy at the grassroots. These are our new, updated and detailed training modules designed especially for field level trainers and include numerous engaging and innovative activities. We are confident that trainers will enjoy using these modules to support women become financially literate and confident. **Your friend and guide**

**Vanita**

**Mann Deshi Foundation**

# Module 7: Investment

## Introduction

This training has already covered the topic of growing one's savings wisely. As mentioned, your savings are secure in the bank where it also earns interest. In addition, it is important to remember that while interest and savings accumulates in a bank, inflation also increases. If we spend ₹ 100 today to buy some goods and services, in a few years, those same goods and services will cost us ₹ 110. Hence, while our money grows in a bank, how much we can buy from that money, or its purchasing power, depends on inflation. In light of this, we need to consider the different ways to grow our money faster than just the interest it earns if it is in a savings account. This module will introduce you to the concept of investment and will discuss issues such as how and where should we invest? What do we need to consider before making any investment decisions and similar topics. ## Objectives

- ❖ Help women to understand the following topics
- ❖ What is investment? - ❖ What are the different types of investment available? - ❖ How does one select the most suitable form of investment? **Duration:** 1 hours 30 minutes

## Process

- ❖ Exercise 1: Suman's Story (Part 7)
- ❖ Exercise 2: The Meaning of Investment
- ❖ Exercise 3: What are the parameters for Investment
- ❖ Game 1: Is this investment option appropriate? - ❖ Exercise 4: Atal Pension Scheme
- ❖ Key Messages

# Exercise 1: Suman’s Story (Part 7)

**Duration:** 10 minutes

## Process

Suman asked Sunitadidi, “You have taught us well. We have started implementing many of your suggestions necessary for financial planning; we have started dividing our needs in four categories and keeping aside money for all these needs. We have understood how to ensure the safety and security of our saving. We have also learned how to accurately calculate our expenses and income, budget and plan for our expenses, reduce unnecessary expenses and stick to our plans and budget. We are also clear that we should buy insurance to protect our savings from getting wiped out if and when there is an emergency. We also realise that we must depend upon our income to take care of our regular needs, our savings to take care of our medium and long term needs and on insurance to cover our emergencies. What is next?”

“Bravo, Suman, you have understood how to protect yourself from a situation of financial deficit. Today you learn about how to grow your wealth so that you have financial surplus,” responded Sunitadidi. ![img-3.jpeg](img-3.jpeg)

## Exercise 2: Meaning of Investment

**Duration:** 10 minutes

**Training material:** Flex

### Process

- ❖ Put the flex on the board. Explain what investment is and how it is beneficial to us with the help of the flex. We save our hard-earned money and keep it in places where it is safe and we get interest on it. Investment, means keeping money for a long time to get more profit on our savings. If we invest money, it grows faster than the savings account. The more the duration, for which the money is kept without withdrawing it, the faster it grows. - ❖ Now show the flex and explain that if today we invest ₹10,000; it grows by ₹ 7,237.00 and becomes ₹ 17,237.00 in six years. If we continue our investment the amount which is ₹ 51,229.00 after 18 years raises to ₹ 88,295 after 24 years. It means in these six years the growth in the money amounts to ₹ 27,066. The money compounds when we start getting interest on previously earned interest in addition to the deposit. Explain that therefore, it is possible to beat inflation if the saving is invested. - ❖ Explain that if we would have kept money in savings account, it would not have grown as much as it has

![img-4.jpeg](img-4.jpeg)

grown now. Explain that hence investment means giving importance to two things. Firstly the more the duration of investment the more the money grows. Secondly, the money should not be withdrawn in between. - ❖ Several options are available for investment. These include buying land, Recurring Deposit (R.D.) Fixed Deposit (F.D.), buying gold, investing in pension schemes etc. We will now see how to decide which of these options will be suitable for us. 4

## Exercise 3: What to Consider Before Investing

**Duration:** 15 minutes

- ❖ Explain to the women that it is important to think through several factors before investing their hard earned money as making an investment means locking money away for a long time. Here's what they need to consider. - ❖ **Profit:** The main objective of an investment is to make a profit and hence it is important to know one's profit margin on the investment. - ❖ **Risk:** Since making an investment means keeping money locked away for a fairly long time period, we must see whether there is any risk of losing our money and what, if any, are the risks involved. There are different types of risks – earning less profit that was expected, not making any profit at all, or losing some or all of our money. It is essential to assess the amount of risk involved before investing your money. - ❖ **Liquidity:** The ease with which any investment can be converted into cash is called liquidity. For some categories of investment, liquidity is high while for others their liquidity is low. It is very important to know whether the investment can be easily converted into cash or else it will be difficult to quickly access your money if you need it urgently. - ❖ **Time:** It is important to think about when you will need the money to achieve a goal. It is one of the primary drivers for your choice of investment type. Some investments make better profits only if they are held for a longer time period. We need to determine where to invest money to meet our long term needs/ goals and where to invest money to meet our short / medium term goals. |  টাক | টাক  |

# Exercise 4: Atal Pension Yojana

**Duration:** 10 minutes

- Ensure that all women have understood the concepts. Whatever money you earn in addition to the money you have invested is called 'Profit'. More the profit, more attractive is the investment option. The possibility of losing the money you have invested is called 'Risk'. Lesser the 'Risk' safer the invested amount. The ease in which any investment can be converted into cash is called 'Liquidity'. More the liquidity, easier the conversion into cash. It means you can get immediate cash at the time when you need it. Time is when we need the money to achieve our goal. Longer the time the investment is continued, the more the growth in the investment. Off course, one cannot think of any of these parameters in isolation as they are dependent on each other. # Guide Book for Financial Literacy

![img-1.jpeg](img-1.jpeg)

## Brief Introduction of the Guide

Mann Deshi is dedicated to the economic empowerment of rural women. It was founded in 1996 in Mhaswad by Chetna Sinha in the drought-prone region of Satara district in Maharashtra. Mann Deshi's vision is to empower women to make their own choices and to be celebrated as equal and valuable members of their families and communities. Our mission is to empower women with the knowledge, skills, courage, access and capital to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. Our model is simple. The Mann Deshi Bank is the country's first cooperative bank set up by and for rural women. Its 8 branches focus on financially excluded and previously unbanked women and provides them with affordable banking services and credit. The Mann Deshi Foundation provides women with the knowledge, skills and support necessary to become successful entrepreneurs with more control over their lives. One of the Foundation's flagship programmes is its business schools for rural women and one of its most important courses is financial literacy. We firmly believe that once women are in control of their finances, entire families and communities can and will be transformed. Financial literacy helps women start their financial journeys – building their savings and assets, being able to access affordable credit and fulfilling their goals. Our experience over the last two decades has sharpened our focus and understanding of how to impart effective financial literacy at the grassroots. These are our new, updated and detailed training modules designed especially for field level trainers and include numerous engaging and innovative activities. We are confident that trainers will enjoy using these modules to support women become financially literate and confident. **Your friend and guide**

**Vanita**

**Mann Deshi Foundation**

# Module 8: Self Help Groups

## Introduction

Today Self Help Groups (SHGs) operate across the country and the number of women involved is growing every day. While there is no mandate that SHGs should only comprise women, it is certainly much more popular with women. However, many women who are SHG members are unsure of how the group is meant to function and this can lead to misinformation, fraud and exploitation. This module covers all the necessary information on how SHGs function and how to benefit from an SHG. ## Objectives

Help women understand the following:

- The benefits of working in a group
- The definition, features and role of Self Help Groups
- How SHGs can empower women

**Duration:** 2 hour 10 minutes

## Process

- Game 1: The difference between working as an individual and in a group
- Exercise 1: Definition and Features of Self Help Groups (SHGs)
- Exercise 2: How Self Help Groups Function
- Exercise 3: The Benefits of Self Help Groups
- Key messages
- Closing
- Suman's story (Final part)

text:
# Game 1: The Difference Between Working as an Individual and in a Group

**Duration:** 20 minutes

**Training material:** 50 pieces of newspaper (one paper of the newspaper could be cut into 4 pieces)

## First round

- ❖ Invite four volunteers to take part in this activity. Make one group with three volunteers and have the fourth volunteer work alone. - ❖ Give the newspaper pieces to both the groups and the volunteer working alone. Tell them to make paper boats. Let them know that they can use any number of pieces to make the boats. However, each boat has to be of the same size and shape. They will start this activity at the same time and both the quantity and quality of the boats will carry the same marks. - ❖ Now invite three other women to participate and ask them to check the quantity and quality of the boats. - ❖ Run the game for five minutes. Ask the groups to count the number of boats that meet the required specifications. ## Discuss the following questions

1. What is the difference between working as an individual and in a group? 2. Which group had produced more boats? Which group produced better quality boats? Why? 3. Has everyone from the group done the same work? 4. What are the benefits of working in a group? 5. Which rules have to be followed if one has to work in the group? 6. What was discussed before starting work? ## Second round

- ❖ Before starting the paper boat making exercise again, give the group (and the lady working alone) time to decide a strategy. Allow five minutes for this round as well. - ❖ Ask the team members in charge of checking quality to count the number of boats that meet the quality requirements and write this down. ## Briefly discuss the following questions

1. Did something different happen this time around? 2. What did they decide before starting the work? Was there any impact of this discussion on the work? ## Discuss the learnings emerging from this game

This should include the following points

- ❖ Working in a group, when done successfully, benefits the quantity and also the quality of work produced. - ❖ Working in a group, when done successfully, allows different members to benefit from each other's different skills since work can be shared and assigned based on different strengths and interests. - ❖ To have a successful group, it is necessary to communicate, make a plan and assign a leader. 3

text:
# Exercise 1: Definition and Features of Self Help Groups (SHGs)

**Duration:** 20 minutes

- ❖ Now explain that the concept of Self Help Groups emerged because of the benefits of working in a group when it came to savings and loans. Since it is often difficult for a woman to save a large sum of money by herself, when many women save together, they have access to a larger pool of money to distribute as loans. **Give the following information about Self Help Groups**

- ❖ The Self Help Groups primarily comprises poor women although there is no rule that Self Help Groups must include only women. Generally a SHG contains 15 or 20 people/ women who willingly come together to form a group with certain definite objectives in mind. - ❖ Usually members of SHG are of a similar financial status and occupation profile. **Self Help Groups have the following the objectives**

- ❖ To mobilize small and fixed savings on a regular basis for a pre-determined period and to use the common pool for internal lending to meet their individual members needs. - ❖ To create and provide a source of income to members to use for productive purposes and help them become self-reliant. - ❖ To be a supportive forum for members and help resolve issues their members might face and also address village or community issues

**The Benefits of Self Help Groups**

- ❖ Members have access to credit at a lower rate of interest compared to a local money lender
- ❖ Members have a supportive forum which promotes a sense of trust and cooperation. - ❖ Members get an opportunity to step out of their houses and learn about new ideas, concepts and opportunities. - ❖ Members learn about various financial services and transactions such as savings, debt, repayment etc. which helps them have greater control over their finances and develops their self-confidence. - ❖ Membership enhances the social status of its individual members in their communities. 4

## Exercise 2: How Self Help Groups Function

**Duration:** 30 minutes

**Training material:** Flip chart of Self-help group. Most rural women are members of one SHG or another and are aware of its basic functions. Ask the participants to present role-plays on how self-help groups work. Form six small groups and ask each group to present a role-play on one of the following topics. ### Topics for the role-play

1. How meetings are held. Present how savings and loan installments are collected during meetings. 2. What is required for SHGs to link with Banks and how this benefits the members? 3. The records and information that SHGs need to maintain. 4. The small business ventures that SHG members work on a group. 5. The support SHGs provide their members for individual business ventures. 6. How decisions are taken within the SHG. ![img-3.jpeg](img-3.jpeg)

After each role-play, include any points which have not been covered during the role play by referring to the SHG Flip Chart. 5

# Exercise 3: The Benefits of Self Help Groups

**Duration:** 30 minutes

**Training material:** Case studies

- ❖ Form three groups and give each a case study. Ask them to discuss their case study – you will give them some questions to consider - and share this with the larger group. ### ❖ Case study 1

Vimal used to stay near the famous Parashuram temple. From a long time, she wanted to start a stall near the temple and sell tea, coffee, kokum juice and mango panna. But she could not do so as she did not have enough money to start. But after being the member of an SHG for six months, she took a ₹ 10,000 loan from her group and her dream finally became a reality. She was also fortunate because her SHG fellow members would bring their guests to Vimal's shop after visiting the temple. She is now considering expanding her business and, as suggested by her SHG members, also adding kokum and jackfruit snacks among her sale items. ![img-4.jpeg](img-4.jpeg)

### ❖ Case study 2

Meena is a member of a Self Help Group. Recently, her son fell off a bicycle while returning from school and fractured his hand. She needed ₹ 2,000 to take him to the hospital for treatment, and when her fellow members found out, they prioritized her problem and gave a loan of ₹ 2,000. 6

text:
# ❖ Case study 3

Prema wants to start her own business. But she is afraid to do it alone. She is concerned that if she is the only one to invest the necessary capital, in case the business fails she will be the only one responsible. She is also not keen to be the only one who runs the businesses and is looking for a partner. ![img-5.jpeg](img-5.jpeg)

When Prema discusses her idea about starting a business with the members of the SHG, most of them are impressed by her idea. They decide to start the business as a collective. They talk about taking a loan from the bank. They also come to know that the Mann Deshi Bank gives loans to SHGs. They take loan from the Mann Deshi Bank and launch their new business. They buy sunflower seeds from the farmers from the village, dry and roast them, pack them in small packets and then sell them as a snack. They share responsibilities and even sell them, fairly successfully, at the Mann Deshi Mahotsav in Satara. Fortunately, they are featured on ABP Maza after which their business really takes off. Ask the group to discuss these case studies and share their thoughts with the larger group. 1. How did the SHG members benefit from being part of the SHG? 2. Apart from increasing savings, how does being a member of a SHG member help women? 3. What impact does SHG membership have on each member's financial position? 7

# Closing

**Duration:** 15 minutes

## Suman’s Story (last part) Puppet Show

**Announcer:** Three years have passed since Suman completed the Mann Deshi Financial Literacy training. In these three years, a lot has changed in her life and the lives of her family. Today let’s go to Dahiwadi and see how Suman is doing. **(Location:** The Mann Deshi Foundation, Dahiwadi office. The Financial Literacy training by Sunitadidi is about to start. Everyone is busy preparing for this.)

**Announcer:** Namaste Sunitadidi. How are the preparations going for the training? **Sunitadidi:** Come… please be seated. What brings you here today? **Announcer:** Guests from Mumbai have come. I have brought them here to meet Suman. Actually, we were going straight to her house but thought we should meet you first. But it seems you are in a hurry. We will come later. We will first meet Suman. **Sunitadidi:** Oh! Why don’t you wait here? Suman will be here any minute. **Announcer:** Thanks but we will just go to her home. (The announcer and the guest move in a circle and reach Suman’s house). **Announcer:** Suman… Suman…

(Two children…Suman’s son and daughter come out of the house). **Suman’s daughter:** Mother has gone out but please come inside. (Suman’s son brings water for them). **Suman’s daughter:** Please be seated. Please wait for some time. Father is on his way. Grandmother is also inside. It’s time for the school bus, so we have to leave. **Guest:** Of course! So both of you go to the school! Where? **Announcer:** Is your school in Dahiwadi? **Suman’s daughter:** Yes… I am in 4$^{th}$ standard and he is in 3$^{rd}$. (They wave goodbye and leave for school)

11
